per_question.question: What medical loss ratio (MLR) must Medicaid managed care organizations meet under federal law, and how does NC implement this requirement?
per_question.agent_answer:
I found the core federal authority: 42 CFR 438.8 governs Medicaid managed care MLR. It says states must require plans to calculate and report MLR, and if a state sets a minimum MLR, it must be at least 85%. I also checked amendments for 42 CFR Part 438; the tool returns the current part as authoritative.

Next I’m looking for North Carolina implementation evidence—ideally state contract/SPA language showing whether NC requires remittances or otherwise operationalizes the federal MLR standard.The NC-specific search in the manual corpus did not surface a clear DHHS or clinical policy section on managed care MLR. The strongest NC implementation evidence in the retrieved materials is the North Carolina CHIP managed care SPA referenced in the frame, plus the federal oversight/remittance provisions in 42 CFR 438.74.

I’m now pulling the full federal oversight section and the NC SPA section text so I can answer how NC implements the requirement without relying on snippets.## Short answer

Under federal Medicaid managed care law, **there is not a universal federally mandated minimum MLR that every Medicaid managed care organization must hit**. Instead, the state must require each MCO/PIHP/PAHP to **calculate and report** an MLR, and **if the state chooses to impose a minimum MLR, that minimum must be at least 85%**. [42 CFR Part 438, § 438.8](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)

For North Carolina, the retrieved implementation evidence shows NC has adopted the federal framework by requiring rates to be designed to reasonably achieve a medical loss ratio and by recognizing the federal remittance/reporting rules if a plan owes money for missing the state’s minimum MLR. [SPA 22-0013 Proposed Amendments CHIP-Managed Care, § 3.3](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/22-0013-proposed-amendment-chip-managed-care/download?attachment)

## Federal rule

### 1) Reporting is mandatory
Federal law requires the state to ensure, through its managed care contracts, that each MCO, PIHP, and PAHP **calculates and reports** an MLR. [42 CFR Part 438, § 438.8(a)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)

### 2) A minimum MLR is optional for the state, but if adopted it must be at least 85%
The key rule is:

- “**If a State elects to mandate a minimum MLR** ... that minimum MLR **must be equal to or higher than 85 percent**.” [42 CFR Part 438, § 438.8(c)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)

So the federal floor is **85%**, but only **when the state chooses to set a minimum MLR requirement**.

### 3) Federal oversight if a state requires remittances
If a state contract requires plans to pay remittances for failing to meet the state minimum MLR, the state must:

- report each plan’s MLR data annually to CMS, including any remittances owed; and
- reimburse CMS for the **federal share** of remittances. [42 CFR Part 438, § 438.74](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)

## How North Carolina implements it

Based on the NC materials I could verify, NC implements the requirement by incorporating the federal managed care MLR structure into its program documents.

The clearest NC text I found says:

- **“The State assures that its rates are designed to reasonably achieve a medical loss”** ratio; and
- if an MCO/PIHP/PAHP owes a remittance for not meeting the minimum MLR required by the state, NC will:
  - reimburse CMS for the federal share, and
  - submit a separate report describing the state/federal share methodology with the annual MLR summary report. [SPA 22-0013 Proposed Amendments CHIP-Managed Care, § 3.3](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/22-0013-proposed-amendment-chip-managed-care/download?attachment)

That aligns directly with the federal oversight/remittance rule in **42 CFR 438.74(b)**. [42 CFR Part 438, § 438.74](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)

## Bottom line

- **Federal law:** Medicaid managed care plans must calculate and report MLR; if a state imposes a minimum MLR, it must be **at least 85%**. [42 CFR Part 438, § 438.8](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)
- **North Carolina implementation:** NC’s retrieved managed care SPA language shows the state uses that federal framework by designing rates to reasonably achieve an MLR and by following the federal remittance/reporting rules when a remittance is owed. [SPA 22-0013 Proposed Amendments CHIP-Managed Care, § 3.3](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/22-0013-proposed-amendment-chip-managed-care/download?attachment)

## Limits / what I could not verify
I **could not verify from the retrieved NC policy corpus** a separate NC manual or contract provision expressly stating, in the text I reviewed, “North Carolina sets the minimum MLR at 85%” for all Medicaid MCOs. The federal rule clearly permits a state minimum of **85% or higher**, and the NC SPA text confirms NC’s use of the federal remittance/reporting structure, but the corpus I searched did not return a clearer NC contract section naming the exact percentage for standard Medicaid managed care contracts.  

I checked amendments for both cited documents, and the tools returned:
- **42 CFR Part 438** as current and authoritative; and
- **SPA 22-0013** as current in the corpus.
